descriptor.scene: Inside the GLOWING ORANGE TRANSLUCENT LAPTOP, FIVE FINISHED BOOKS float in a loose row, and EVERY ONE OF THEM IS A DIFFERENT WORLD: five different page shapes, five different painting styles, five different letterings, nothing shared between any two. Warm evening light. CAMERA: THIS IS AN OVER-THE-SHOULDER SHOT. The camera sits BEHIND AND SLIGHTLY ABOVE MARCUS, who is SEATED IN HIS CHAIR at the desk. We look PAST THE BACK OF HIS HEAD AND ONE SHOULDER, which occupy the near foreground at the lower left, straight at the glowing screen, so the viewer sees exactly what he sees. HIS FACE IS NOT VISIBLE AT ALL: we see the back of his head, his dark hair greying at the temples with the wire-rimmed glasses pushed up into it, and the shoulder of his soft OLIVE-GREEN shirt. He is NOT turned toward the camera and NOT seen from the side. The screen is the subject and should hold the centre of the frame.

prompt: Picture-book spread painted in the warm editorial ink-and-wash register of the FIRST reference image. THE FIRST REFERENCE IMAGE IS A STYLE ANCHOR ONLY. Match it for MEDIUM, BRUSHWORK, PALETTE and LIGHT QUALITY ONLY, and take NO subject from it whatsoever: none of its objects, figures, costume, props, furniture, architecture, period or location may appear in the output unless the scene description below asks for them by name. WARM EDITORIAL INK-AND-WASH illustration: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent watercolour washes over it, a muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the look of a thoughtful printed picture book for adults. It is NOT neon, NOT 3D or CGI or Pixar, NOT glossy plastic, NOT neo-comic, and carries NO HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary. ONE single full-bleed scene per image: never a grid, never split panels, never a contact sheet, never a before-and-after. This is a quiet account of working out what a children's book is actually made of, set in an ordinary family house. Each spread contains ONLY the figures its own scene description names. Keep the LOWER RIGHT of the frame calm and uncluttered, because a caption card sits there. MARCUS, a man in his LATE THIRTIES, ordinary and a little tired. SHORT DARK HAIR going GREY AT THE TEMPLES and a few days of STUBBLE. A soft OLIVE-GREEN SHIRT worn open over a plain GREY TEE, sleeves rolled to the forearm. WIRE-RIMMED READING GLASSES, often pushed up onto his head rather than worn. He is a MARKETER and a dad, NOT an engineer: never a hoodie, never a startup uniform, never a technologist, never a wall of monitors. He is patient, curious and slightly rumpled. He is ALWAYS in the warm real room and NEVER inside the laptop screen. Warm-editorial ink-and-wash on a cream ground, never photoreal, never 3D, never glossy. SITTING BACK from the desk, glasses pushed up into his hair, one hand over his mouth, looking at nothing in particular. Genuinely stuck, NOT despairing and NOT theatrical. marcus-study exactly as its reference plate: THE STUDY: a corner of an ordinary family house that has been turned into a desk, not a room built for work. A plain wooden table against a wall under a sash window, a mismatched dining chair, a shelf of well-read children's picture books, a mug, a radiator, a child's drawing stuck to the wall with tape. Warm lamplight and whatever comes through the window. The rest of the house is visible past a doorway: a hallway, a bit of sofa, toys on the floor. NEVER an office, NEVER a studio, NEVER a wall of monitors, NEVER a whiteboard covered in diagrams, NEVER impressive. HANDEDNESS IS FIXED. The desk stands against the wall under the WINDOW, and the camera is always INSIDE the room at seated eye height, over Marcus's shoulder or beside him in three-quarter view. THE GLOWING LAPTOP SITS ON THE DESK AND ITS SCREEN FACE IS ALWAYS VISIBLE TO THE VIEWER, never the back of the lid. Marcus is always OUTSIDE the laptop, in the room. The doorway to the rest of the house is at the camera's LEFT and never moves. DEFAULT CAMERA IS OVER-THE-SHOULDER, and this is a correction of a real authoring bias. On any spread where THE SCREEN IS THE SUBJECT, the camera sits BEHIND AND SLIGHTLY ABOVE Marcus's shoulder while he is SEATED, so the viewer looks past the back of his head and his shoulder at the glowing screen and sees what he sees. His face is not visible in those shots and does not need to be. Reserve the side-on three-quarter view, where his face reads, for the spreads whose subject is HIS REACTION rather than the screen. The book argues that he is outside the machine looking in, and over-the-shoulder is the composition that says so; side-on quietly turns it into a man talking to a gadget. LIVED-IN and domestic: a cooling mug, a child's crayon drawing taped to the wall, a stack of picture books with broken spines, a stray sock or toy on the floor past the doorway, cables that are just cables. It is NEVER tidy, NEVER styled, and NEVER lit dramatically. RENDER ONE MOMENT IN TIME ONLY: one view of one room, never a before-and-after, never a split panel. A corner of a house. Small enough that a man at a desk fills it. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic, NO STRAY OR INVENTED TEXT anywhere: no captions, no labels, no signage, no watermarks, no logos, no signatures, no dates, no readable handwriting and no readable print. Writing on paper or on a screen is PICTORIAL SCRIBBLE ONLY and must never resolve into words., NO PHYSICAL FACTORY: no warehouse, no conveyor belt, no industrial machinery, no robot arms, no server racks and no assembly hall anywhere in this book. Every factory is inside the laptop screen., MARCUS IS NEVER INSIDE THE LAPTOP SCREEN and never shrunk, never floating in it, never reaching into it. He stays in the real room., NEVER show the back of a laptop lid, and never the lid-back and the screen face in the same image. The screen face is always toward the viewer., THE ROOM IS NEVER AN OFFICE, a studio, a startup, a lab or a maker-space. No wall of monitors, no whiteboard covered in diagrams, no exposed brick, no neon sign, no lanyards., NOTHING IS TRIUMPHANT: no fist-pumps, no applause, no crowds, no pitch decks, no stage, no trophy. Nobody is lit from below or haloed., THE SUPERCHARGED LAPTOP LAW, and it is canon: when an agent is running, the ENTIRE LAPTOP is a TRANSLUCENT LUMINOUS HOLOGRAPHIC OBJECT, glowing all through its lid, its keyboard, its base and its edges, so you can SEE THROUGH the whole machine and it casts light rather than shadow. It is NEVER an ordinary solid laptop with a bright screen. If the body of the machine looks like normal grey metal or plastic while only the display glows, the image has failed., LAPTOP SCALE IS FIXED AND IT IS SMALL: an ordinary 14-inch notebook, 33cm wide with 21cm of screen when open. Its open screen is only about TWICE THE HEIGHT OF THE MUG on the desk beside it, and the whole machine takes up only about a QUARTER of the desk's width. It is NEVER as tall as a person's head and shoulders, NEVER half the desk, NEVER a monitor, NEVER a television. Whatever is happening inside the screen has DEPTH but the screen itself stays a small ordinary rectangle.. ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind.
